MOVE-PROFILE-AUTHORING. **Proposal and evidence only**, per Astra's Cycle 2 handoff: "missing policy/cost values stay explicitly unresolved until the Q2 ruling." Nothing here answers Q2, authors a profile, or closes a movement gate.

## The register

**35 Q2 slots, every value `null`** — 5 measured envelope inputs, 11 cost-row fields, 8 safety bindings, 6 geometry extents, 5 policy questions only Astra can answer. Each carries its units, its owning contract, and what it is currently blocking, so Astra can rule on an inventory rather than reconstruct one.

**288 rows** (16 species × 3 life stages × 6 modes): **8 adopted, 0 explicitly_disabled, 280 unresolved_q2, 0 admission_qualified.** The 64 adult connected rows and the 8 ground/ford `S/N` cells reconcile exactly with MOVE-C2-R01's own counts.

Both the matrix and the totals were **rebuilt and re-asserted at write time** rather than transcribed, and the file's own `validator_rules` are asserted before it is written: every leaf resolves to a row class, no row's `blocking_contract` has `kind: presentation`, no `presentation_gaps` id appears in any `evidence_absent`, and no slot carries a value.

## Two new questions

**Q2-24 — `FORD_WALK` has an id and a bit but no behaviour.** `_cursor_mode` is written at `_attach_route()` and read only by `admitted_mode_of()`; no cell predicate, cost or eligibility rule consults it. Ford and ground walk are today the same traversal with different labels. `world_init.gd` does define a ford geometrically (`is_ford()`, river tiles z = 48..51, `FORD_Y_UNITS = -128`), but that is inherited GDD §5.1 map geometry, not a movement policy, and no per-profile water-depth limit exists anywhere.

**Q2-32 — does HAZ-001's CHILD prohibition reach travel?** It forbids CHILD hazardous *work* and excavation, and classifies dive, swim and unprotected climb as dangerous. Whether a child may *travel* those modes is stated nowhere. That single unanswered question is what prevents 48 CHILD rows from being classified either way — and they stay `unresolved_q2` rather than being upgraded to `explicitly_disabled` by inference.

## It found real envelope data and refused to use it

`godot/assets/lookdev/proportion_comparison_manifest.json` **does** carry per-pose horizontal and vertical extents for five species. Recorded as `EV-BLOCKOUT-POSE-BOUNDS` and disqualified on five independent grounds, any one sufficient: hand-authored blockout rather than reviewed production geometry; `landmark_status: PROPOSED_FOR_REVIEW`; MOVE-C2-R01's explicit proxy exclusion; discrete rest poses rather than a sweep with an error bound; and no margin or declared anchor-to-root offset, which Q1 §3 makes disqualifying on its own.

That is the "already exists" trap this project has been caught by before — found, named, and neither used nor pretended away.

## Two claims in our own planning docs are false today

`movement_starter_ground_profile.md` asserts `residents.gd` has no life-stage column and that `SpeciesDefinition.rig_id` has no values. **Both exist.** Treated as historical and not repeated.

Reported, not edited: `docs/planning/asset_dimensions_and_budgets.md` lists squirrel at 1024 u against DEC-039's approved **1178**, which the lookdev manifest already carries. Another lane's file.

## The separation it binds itself to

> A missing rig is a presentation/export gap. A missing clearance, profile or contact contract is a movement **admission** blocker. They must refuse differently, and neither may be substituted for the other.

All sixteen rig identities exist and **close nothing here** — a logical rig identity is not a capability. Conversely no missing mesh or clip appears anywhere as a reason a species cannot use a mode; those live only in `presentation_gaps`, which no admission validator reads. `BC-RIG` is declared `kind: presentation` specifically so a validator can assert it never appears as a row's blocker.

## Not claimed

No dimension, cost, speed, air budget, depth or clearance value is authored. No route recentring is proposed — production placement stays `(+256,+256)`. MOVE-G01–G05, 05.1b and the `MOVE-ENVELOPES` inbox item are unchanged. No paid generation is authorized.

SURVIVED_MUTANTS: none

RENDER-SPAWN, implementing INIT-POSE-R01. `settlement_system.gd` now composes **one** `transforms.gd` bound to the same EntityDirectory as the resident store; the renderer borrows it. `resident_pose_scaffold.gd` is **deleted whole**, and its test with it.

## The ledger shrinks — the first negative row in this project

The arithmetic is exact rather than approximate: §2.2's `Transform` rows (2,801,664) plus §3's `TransformBinding` (350,208) = **3,151,872**, which is precisely what the scaffold duplicated. Nothing moved; bytes were removed.

| Identity | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Allocation rows | 31 | **30** |
| Planned payload | 72,110,995 | **68,959,123** |
| One live world plus reserve | 80,499,603 | **77,347,731** |
| Headroom below 100 MB | 19,500,397 | **22,652,269** |
| Transactional peak | 146,395,014 | **140,091,270** |

Decision 0130's `+3203072` step stays — only its second row is removed, and the 51,200 instance-buffer row it also added remains.

## It found a crash in the merge gate

`check_trail` parsed `int(delta.lstrip("+"))`. A **U+2212 MINUS SIGN** — visually identical to ASCII `-` in a diff, and the obvious thing to paste from a document — raised `ValueError` out of the check, which reads as a *broken gate* rather than a bad row. That is the worse of the two failures.

It now refuses with the row, the value and the likely cause named. `test_merge_gate.py` gains both cases: a valid negative delta chains and passes; a Unicode minus refuses. Neither had ever been exercised, because until now **every row in this ledger added bytes**.

The lane hit this and worked around it with ASCII. The tool should not have needed the workaround.

## Placement

Initial cohort ordered by persistent ID, `i = persistent_id - 1`: exterior tile `(58+i, 69)`, root x `119808 + 2048*i`, y `512`, z `142336`, yaw `0`, previous equal to current. The hall's south apron — outside its `12x10` footprint, granting no home assignment.

**`world_init.gd` is byte-identical to base**, verified by `git diff --quiet` and `shasum`. The clear mask *already* reserved the row: `is_cleared_tile()` includes `is_starter_apron_tile()`, whose hall ring covers x=57..70, z=58..69. No new reservation was needed and none was invented.

## Mutations: 17 run, 17 killed

Four survived the first pass and got **tests**, not equivalence claims. `refuse_assembly_occupancy()` and `resolve_assembly_order_into()` were made static and store/world-injected purely so fixtures can execute branches that are unreachable on a production world — on a real world an id-order rule and a slot-order rule are indistinguishable. Recorded in ADR 0138 rather than left as an unexplained signature.

Disclosed unprompted: an earlier sequence was interrupted mid-mutation by the lane's own edit to a frozen file, leaving one `world_init.gd` mutant applied. It was restored from git, SHA-256 compared, every contaminated verdict discarded, and the 17 rows come from a single clean sequence over a frozen tree.

## Evidence

```
./tools/run_tests.sh
state_registry_coverage: PASS -- 54 modules, 352 rows, 681 packed columns checked
4355 test(s), 155623 assertion(s), 0 failure(s)
```

Captures in `docs/validation/evidence/resident-render-path/authoritative-spawn/`. The harness printed `store settlement==stage true  settlement==crowd true  bound=12` — reference identity, one object — and capture `04` raises resident 1 by 2048 units, showing it visibly lifted with its shadow at `instance 0 origin (117.0, 2.5, 139.0)`. That is the proof the renderer reads the authoritative store rather than a copy.

## Not claimed

**No visual acceptance.** The cohort still draws as one untextured bind-pose mouse mesh, and the −Z-forward facing question needs a human eye. Species, material, rig and facing validation are a separate presentation lane.

Owed downstream, not merge-blocking: the §4 Transform save codec round trip for a resident whose previous and current differ, and the rules-identity revision in `canonical_state_registry.json`, which another lane owned at the time.

There is **no definition for persistent ID 13+**. Immigration, births, rescue release, load and scenario variants need their own placement contracts, and later arrivals must not reuse the assembly row instead of the map exit `(64,126)`.

Recorded as ADR 0138.

body:
MOVE-ENVELOPE-TOOLING, implementing MOVE-C2-R01's measurement method. **This is tooling, not measurements** — no body dimension is invented, and every number in the fixtures is synthetic and refused if it claims otherwise.

## The result Astra required, proved rather than asserted

`compute_fit` returns four distinguishable refusals. For a negative translated minimum it returns `PLACEMENT_INCOMPATIBLE_AT_OFFSET`, never `CLEARANCE_CLASS_EXCEEDS_DOMAIN` — and it **proves** it by scanning the whole 1..512 domain:

```
PLACEMENT_INCOMPATIBLE_AT_OFFSET  synthetic_specimen_alpha/ADULT/GROUND_WALK/... [synthetic_fixture]
   local x[-418..418] z[-418..418] -> translated x[-162..674] z[-162..674] at offset (256, 256)
   translated minimum below the north-west anchor. The clearance square grows SOUTH and EAST
   from its anchor, so no clearance class repairs this: 0 of the 512 published classes admit
   these bounds. A naive ceil(max(width,depth)/cell) would have answered class 2, which is
   exactly the lower bound MOVE-C2-R01 §4 says never replaces containment.
```

Naming the wrong answer it would otherwise have given is the part that makes this useful: someone reading `class 2` would go hunting for a k that cannot exist.

`FitResult.require_class()` raises on any refused fit — there is **no sentinel class**. Re-centring is neither proposed nor implemented; a non-baseline offset is accepted report-only and printed as `(NOT baseline: report only)`.

## It reads the constants instead of restating them

`spatial_world.gd` is byte-unchanged. The validator parses `CELL_SIZE_UNITS`, `CELL_CENTRE_OFFSET_UNITS`, `MIN/MAX_CLEARANCE_CLASS` and `CELLS_X/Z` out of it, mode ids out of `movement.gd`, and life-stage ids out of `residents.gd` — and **refuses a record file whose `convention` block disagrees with the parsed source.** A restated constant is a constant that drifts.

## No dimension can masquerade as a measurement

Every number is a synthetic constant under `synthetic_specimen_alpha`. A record with `data_class: synthetic_fixture` is **refused if it carries provenance**, and a `measurement` is refused if it lacks it — so a fixture cannot be read as a body dimension in either direction. Measured extrema are exact signed integer micrometres; there is no float in the schema, validator or tests.

## Evidence

```
python3 tools/test_movement_envelopes.py
test_movement_envelopes: PASS -- 124 check(s), 0 failure(s)

./tools/run_tests.sh
4338 test(s), 152837 assertion(s), 0 failure(s)
```

Exit codes verified independently: naming no record file exits **1** ("validating nothing is not a pass"); the placement-incompatible fixture exits **2**; each malformed fixture exits **1**.

**19 mutants, 19 killed**, one per invocation with a `shasum -a 256` byte-compare after each restore. Coverage includes the anchor offset dropped, quantization rounded inward on both bounds, the class bound and ceiling division off by one, the negative minimum misreported as a class problem, the placement check removed, and `require_class()` returning `-1` instead of refusing.

The lane corrected its own lane record, which said "seventeen" — the true count is 19 including two schema mutants. It also flagged that M1 initially killed only via an uncaught `TypeError`, so `main()` now records a crash as a failure rather than losing the summary line.

## CI gap closed here

`tools/test_movement_envelopes.py` was not in the workflow, which the lane reported as outside its allowlist. Now wired into the `contracts` job.

Recorded as [ADR 0141](docs/decisions/0141-a-placement-refusal-is-not-a-clearance-class-refusal.md).

**No movement gate is closed.** MOVE-C2-R01 Q2 per-species rows remain open and nothing here authors a profile.

Transfers Astra's Cycle 2 package and reconciles the queue with what has merged since its PR snapshot. **No implementation, no art approval, no credit authorization.**

## Two blockers answered, one partially

| Question | Ruling | Lane |
|---|---|---|
| Retired inventory rows vs the canonical digest | **INV-CANON-R01** — normalize unused payloads in the quiescent save/hash copy; preserve live values, generations and used free-stack order; never clear source attributes during hot retirement | DIGEST-DETERMINISM |
| Container enumeration / stranded goods | **INV-GOODS-R01** — a bounded owner query, plus a real demolition coordinator that proves complete affected endpoints and rechecks goods/claims/occupants. Real hauling precedes demolition | CONSTRUCTION-GOODS |
| MOVE-G01 Q1/Q2 | **MOVE-C2-R01** — retain classes 1–512, measure swept body/gear/load bounds, quantize outward, prove fit against the actual north-west anchor. **Q2 production profiles remain open** | MOVE-ENVELOPE-TOOLING + MOVE-PROFILE-AUTHORING; MOVE-ENVELOPES stays gated |

## The finding that prevents a wrong implementation

A blanket retirement clear — the obvious reading of "blank retired rows" — is **unsafe** in the current algorithm. `_apply_transfer()` retires the source *before* `_credit_new_lot()` reads its attributes, and with one free lot slot the same slot is reused with a new generation. The save/hash adapter must not mutate those runtime bytes; normalization belongs in the quiescent copy.

Also: generation MAX is **not** synonymous with retirement. A slot freed from MAX−1 is pushed at MAX for its final valid reuse, so free-MAX, live-MAX and retired-MAX are three distinct states, and prefix membership plus occupancy is what distinguishes them.

And a reachable state the merged §7 codec would reject: reserving 250 milli-U on a 1000 lot then merging into a compatible 1000 lot leaves the dead source at quantity 0 / reserved 250 while the live destination correctly holds reserved 250. An unconditional `reserved <= quantity` check rejects it. The new projection writes dead `reserved=0` while retaining the live claim.

## Queue reconciliation

Astra's queue was computed against a base older than master, so `git apply --3way` conflicted on all five shared planning files. The planner's versions are authoritative for Cycle 2, so they were taken whole and corrected for three landings its PR snapshot predates: PACKET-EVIDENCE done (#117), SAVE-REGISTRY-RECONCILE done (#119), ART-UI-12-EVIDENCE in review (#118).

**RENDER-SPAWN is marked `in_flight`.** It was dispatched before Cycle 2 landed and is still running, and it owns `settlement_system.gd` and its test — which CONSTRUCTION-GOODS also claims. Without that mark the dispatcher offered both at once, which is exactly the collision the ownership rule exists to prevent. The queue now withholds CONSTRUCTION-GOODS and offers three lanes rather than four.

## One pin relaxed, with its reason

Astra's own `validate_cycle02_handoff.py` required `PACKET-EVIDENCE` to be `review` with pr 117 — a snapshot of its PR-query moment. #117 has since merged, so that pin would fail on a tree that is *more* correct than the one it was written against. The PR number is the durable half and stays exact; the status may advance, since a lane only moves forward from review. Same distinction as `packed_source_field_count`: a snapshot REG-R01 requires to grow is not a format constant.

## Evidence

`merge_gate` · `ready07_arithmetic` · `decision_numbers` (132) · `lane_notes` · `state_registry_coverage` · `validate_save_registry_handoff --source-root .` · `generate_canonical_state_table --check` · `dispatch_plan --validate` (27 tasks) · `astra_inbox --check` · Astra's `validate_cycle02_handoff` (37 checks) — all PASS.

Astra separately ran a focused Godot probe against unchanged local Inventory, byte-identical to PR116: **14 checks, 0 failures**. Its two failed preliminary attempts are preserved in the package, including one whose exit helper could print success after an assertion — diagnostic-harness errors, not production fixes.

Recorded as ADR 0140.

SAVE-REGISTRY-RECONCILE, Astra Cycle 1 step 2. Astra called this "a concrete unrecorded schema omission ... that must be repaired, not accepted as an exclusion."

Seventeen `construction.gd` packed columns existed in code and in `docs/persistence_state_registry.md`, classified as persistent state, and were **absent from `canonical_state_registry.json`**. No gate was looking — Astra found it by reading the tree.

## What landed

16 project columns as `(4, "construction", v1)` and `_delivered_milli` as `(5, "construction", v1)`, all `hash: true`, under one new contract key **C172** — computed as `max(int(k[1:]))+1` from the file, because a previous lane proposed a key that was already taken. Types read off the GDScript; capacities quote `CONSTRUCTION_CAPACITY = 82944` and `DELIVERED_CELLS = 331776`.

`_present` takes **ordinal 0** under ARCH-SAVE-002's occupied-bitset-first rule, even though `construction.gd` declares it after `_material_container_slot`. `(4,"needs")` and `(4,"buildings")` already carry the same hoist.

## Both pins moved, and for a different reason than last time

`record_count` 582 → **599**, `packed_source_field_count` 536 → **553**.

Decision 0133's eight `event_schedule` fields were *already declared* before their module existed, so that landing moved the packed count alone. Construction's seventeen were **never declared**, so they are seventeen new `hash: true` declarations and `record_count` follows. That contrast is written beside both numbers in the validator and the test, not just the digits — confusing the two is how a snapshot becomes a format constant that refuses every new store.

## The mutant that justifies the new tests

**G5**: the registry reordered into `construction.gd`'s declaration order *and the table regenerated consistently*. The Python validator passed and **every pre-existing Godot test passed.** Those tests only prove the table and the JSON agree — they cannot see the two agreeing about the wrong thing. The new `test_construction_section_four_columns_are_declared_in_order` pins key order and type codes as literal constants and was the sole failure.

That is the same symmetric-blindness shape as §7's `_read_block()` and §9's ordinal swap.

12 mutants, 12 killed, one per Godot invocation, every file `shasum -a 256` byte-compared after restore.

## A generator that proved the hand-maintained table had already drifted

`tools/generate_canonical_state_table.py` is new. `canonical_state_hash.gd`'s header has named it since ADR 0127 but it never existed, so 590 entries were hand-maintained. Run against the **pre-change** registry it reproduced the checked-in table byte for byte except one number: the header said "530 persisted packed fields" when the registry had said 536 since decision 0133.

## The CI gap this exposed — fixed here

`.github/workflows/tests.yml` ran `state_registry_coverage.py` but **not** `validate_save_registry_handoff.py`, the check that compares the registry against the GDScript backing it. `--source-root .` is the load-bearing half; without it the validator only checks the artifact against itself.

Both now run in the `contracts` job — pure Python, no engine, no LFS, 0.2s. **Verified as a negative:** removing one construction column's declaration makes both new steps exit 1; restoring it makes both exit 0, with the registry byte-identical by `shasum`.

## Evidence

```
PASS source membership/types: 553 persisted packed fields
PASS registry structure: 52 owners, 599 canonical records
PASS generated declaration table matches canonical_state_registry.json
state_registry_coverage: PASS -- 54 modules, 352 rows, 681 packed columns checked
decision_numbers: PASS -- 130 records
merge_gate: PASS
ok: 4338 tests, 152837 assertions, 0 failures.
```

## Scope deliberately not claimed

**R-WORLD-S1-001 untouched** — `resource_nodes`' three deposit members are still declared, its `owner_schema_version` is 1, `section_schema_versions[0]` is 2. That ruling's "−3 only" figures of 579/533 were explicitly forbidden as final pins; the integrated totals are 599/553, which is what it asked for. SAVE-S1-OWNERS activates that migration atomically.

No section or owner version movement: both new blocks are additions at `owner_schema_version 1`, no existing owner's field set changed, and no §4 or §5 codec exists to pin either number against.

No adapter — `production_walker()` still refuses `CANONICAL_NO_ADAPTER`, now listing 52 owners.

`source_module_sha256` left stale **on purpose**: nine of its 47 entries already disagree with the tree and seven core modules are absent from it. It is a 197472b snapshot, and half-refreshing it would make it look current.

Recorded as ADR 0137.

ART-UI-12-EVIDENCE, Astra Cycle 1. **Evidence only — no visual approval is claimed or granted anywhere in this change. ART-UI-12 remains Brendan's verdict.**

Astra found the existing captures insufficient: "the roster-over-alert and clipped-counter examples fail the intended readable shell." Rather than re-shoot the 40 captures that already exist, this closes the two gaps they cannot answer.

**This branch changes no `godot/` file.** Measured against the merge base, which is the correct measure: `git diff $(git merge-base origin/master HEAD) HEAD -- godot/` is empty. An earlier revision of this body said `git diff origin/master HEAD -- godot/`, which was true when written and became false the moment #119 merged and changed two `canonical_state_hash` files on master. The lane caught that; a moving tip is not a baseline. `art_approvals.json` and `docs/design/ui_refinement/` are untouched. No credits spent.

## Counter clipping: arithmetic, not anecdote

Text budget = cell width − 24 px icon − 2+2 px style margins − 4 px separation = **77.33 px STANDARD / 72.00 px NARROW**.

Two facts the existing 40 captures did not carry:

- **No populated counter fits** at 1280×720 at any of the three user scales — two digits maximum at STANDARD.
- **The bare word `Residents` measures 86.00 px**, so that cell overflows **with no value in it at all**.

Capture `03` puts the boundary in one frame: `Food 1` and `Wood 12` whole, `Stone 123` → `Stone 12`, `Residents 1234` → `Resident`.

## Occlusion: measured, not inferred from a flag

Previously this rested on cards reporting `visible = true`. Captures are bit-deterministic (same mode twice → 0 differing pixels of 921600), so the comparison is exact:

| Pair | Differing pixels |
|---|---|
| `10` vs `11` — alert expired vs active, workspace open | **0 of 14080** over card 0's rect `(462,18,320,44)`; **0 of 11520** over card 1's band |
| `11` vs `12` — workspace open vs closed, alert active | 2829 and 2641 |

The cards are placed, report visible, and draw **zero pixels** while the workspace is open.

## A third condition found and deliberately not captured

The same unstated §1.2 precedence puts **216 of the resources rectangle's 360 px**, and the minimap frame from x=160, inside the modal rectangle `(160,16,960,688)`. Already visible in existing capture `40`, merely unremarked — so it is named with arithmetic in the README rather than re-shot.

## Reproducibility

```
godot --headless --path godot --editor --quit            # mandatory first, fresh worktree
godot --path godot --script capture_artui12_scratch.gd --resolution 1280x720 \
    -- <ABSOLUTE-out.png> <mode> <scale>
godot --headless --path godot --script diff_artui12_scratch.gd -- <a.png> <b.png> <x y w h>
```

Every run wrapped in `perl -e 'alarm 240; exec @ARGV'`. Modes per file are tabulated in the README.

Suite on the final tree: `ok: 4336 tests, 152719 assertions, 0 failures.`

DEVIATIONS: (1) a third occlusion frame was shot — the workspace-closed control `12` — because a bare with/without pair cannot distinguish "occluded" from "the card drew nothing"; (2) the `ladder` mode supplies value magnitudes through `ui_shell.set_counter_display()`, the only harness-supplied content in the set, labelled as such in the README, with all nine other captures carrying store-derived or boot values only; (3) the per-cell fit diagnostic returned `-1` when a bare label already overflowed its budget — a sentinel standing in for a count, against the house rule — and now prints `value_digits_that_fit=none, the bare label already overflows`. Printed diagnostic only; the byte-identical reproduction of capture 03 proves no pixel depends on it. Integration note: the lane's commits were authored with a private email GitHub refused to publish and were rewritten to the `users.noreply.github.com` address every other commit here uses; content unchanged. Astra accepted (1) and (2) in Cycle 2 as "reasonable evidence choices".

Astra asked for the deleted capture/diff scripts back so the evidence is reproducible from repository contents. They now live at `docs/validation/harnesses/artui12/`, and the README's command blocks name the path they invoke.

The lane **measured** rather than assumed that Godot 4.7.2 resolves `--script` outside the project directory — both the relative and absolute forms produce identical output — so no file sits loose in `godot/` and there is no copy-in step.

body:
PACKET-EVIDENCE, Astra Cycle 1. Two problems, one root cause: the review packet was auditing the wrong thing, and two separate parsers disagreed about what a declaration means.

## The packet was not auditing pull requests

It read **local HEAD commit bodies**, used `git log --merges` (which omits squash merges entirely), and could not see work merged after the local ref. It then reported "None in this window" — which Astra correctly called unsupported: of 103 in-window merged PRs, it listed 50, missed 49 reachable from cached master, and three more it could not reach at all.

Now sourced from merged PR bodies via `gh pr list --search`, with pagination by **time bisection** — that API has no cursor, so a sub-window returning exactly `--limit` rows is split into overlapping halves and re-queried, and a saturated one-second window **raises** rather than silently returning short. Verified live: the same 105 records at `--limit 100` (3 sub-queries) and at `--limit 10` (37 sub-queries).

The packet now states which ref and window it covered, how many records it saw, and what it could not see — so it can no longer present *no evidence* as *no exceptions*.

## The grammar: five outcomes, not two

```
CLEAR      <- normalises to exactly "none"
MALFORMED  <- normalises to empty
QUALIFIED  <- begins "none" + non-word char, with anything else remaining
DECLARED   <- anything else
MISSING    <- no declaration line for that block
```

**`none — <explanation>` is QUALIFIED, and that is the load-bearing choice.** The two constraints admit no binary answer. Calling it empty means `SURVIVED_MUTANTS: none — M7 is still alive, we shipped anyway` clears the gate. Calling it non-empty is what misreported #103 and #104, which both describe mutants that *died*. No regex separates those strings — the difference is in the meaning of prose. So the parser refuses to decide: QUALIFIED is neither cleared nor counted as a survivor; it is printed in full in its own section that says only a human can grade it.

Deliberate consequences: `n/a` is DECLARED (only the literal `none` clears — widening the vocabulary widens the hiding place); a lowercase `deviations:` is MISSING, so casing-evasion lands in the *louder* bucket; multiple lines take the **most severe** outcome, so a trailing `DEVIATIONS: none` cannot cancel a real one above it; `|` is excluded from the margin, so a docs table naming the blocks is a specification, not a declaration.

## The hole this exposed in the merge gate

`auto_merge.py` kept its own parser for the same three blocks, and it used `re.search` — **the first match wins.** A real exception written below an earlier `none` was invisible and the PR merged:

```
DEVIATIONS: none
...
DEVIATIONS: overruled the brief, shipped anyway   <- never seen
```

Demonstrated against the old code before replacing it. `check_report` now calls `review_packet.parse_declarations`. Two parsers for one grammar is how the two drift.

| case | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| honest `none` | merges | merges |
| real exception after a quoted `none` | **merges** | holds |
| bare blocks, no content | holds | holds |
| qualified `none` | merges | holds |
| genuine survivor | holds | holds |

**One correction to the lane's report:** it stated a bare `DEVIATIONS:` auto-merges today. It does not — the old pattern's greedy `\s*` swallows the newline and captures the following line. The ordering hole is the one that actually bites. Checked empirically rather than by reading.

## Mutations

16 run, one per invocation, byte-compared after each restore. **14 killed first time; 2 survived and exposed real test gaps:**

- *margin admits `|`* survived — the fixture had prose before the block name, never exercising the pipe exclusion. Two table-cell fixtures added. Killed.
- *`_cell` truncates to 40 chars* survived — the "in full" assertion only checked a prefix. Replaced with character-for-character containment plus "no `…` anywhere in the packet". Killed.

No test weakened or deleted.

## Evidence

```
review_packet self-test: 67 case(s), 0 failure(s) -- PASS
review_packet: 103 PR record(s) from snapshot; 2 declared, 2 qualified, 0 malformed, 282 missing block(s)
state_registry_coverage: PASS -- 54 modules, 352 rows, 681 packed columns checked
4336 test(s), 152719 assertion(s), 0 failure(s)
```

The self-test replays the preserved corpus and reproduces Astra's counts exactly: 103 records, 9 with all three blocks, 94 with none.

Recorded as ADR 0139.

Astra Cycle 1, step 1. Astra reviewed a working snapshot, Git HEAD pointed at a much older commit, and merged master was ahead of both. Every Cycle 1 lane needs to know which is authoritative for what — so this records it once rather than having each lane rediscover it.

## The reconciliation

| | |
|---:|---|
| **1413** | identical between the reviewed snapshot and merged master |
| **51** | master-only — §7/§12 codecs and lane records merged after the snapshot |
| **12** | diverged — **master newer in all twelve**; nothing in the snapshot was ahead |
| **0** | local-only tracked files |
| **17** | untracked — the only genuinely new content, transferred here |
| **11** | Astra's unstaged edits, applied with `git apply --3way` **per file** so one failure could not abort the rest. All eleven clean. |

## Brendan's work was not touched

The staged index is preserved as a **reachable commit** at `refs/wip/baseline-2026-09-14`, written with `commit-tree` so it cannot be garbage-collected. The working tree still reports the same 341 changed paths it did before this lane started. Nothing was mass-committed — its content is already in master.

## Four ADR collisions, resolved by comparing content

Astra and the executor allocate decision numbers from separate sessions with no shared counter, so collisions are the expected outcome rather than bad luck.

The untracked `0090`/`0091`/`0092` turned out to be **stale pre-renumber copies** of decisions master already carries as `0097`/`0106`/`0107` — two byte-identical below the heading, and the third differing only by a provenance note master already carries *describing that very renumber*. Dropped as superseded, which is not the same as deleting an unexplained copy.

Astra's cycle-one ADR is genuinely new and took **0136**, since 0135 is the merged lane-records decision.

### I got that wrong first

The initial pass renumbered the three stale copies to 0136/0137/0138, **creating a third copy of each decision**. It was caught only by reading the queue's own `owns` list, which already named 0097/0106/0107 as the live numbers. Reverted before commit.

The ruling said to resolve duplicates *by comparing contents*. I renumbered first and compared after; doing it in the stated order would have caught this immediately. It is recorded in the manifest rather than quietly fixed.

## Reproduced, deliberately not fixed

`validate_save_registry_handoff.py --source-root .` fails exactly as Astra reported: **17 `construction.gd` packed fields** classified as persistent state but absent from `canonical_state_registry.json`. That is `SAVE-REGISTRY-RECONCILE`'s owned work.

Neither fails a test; neither is investigated here. `CLEAN-SHUTDOWN` is in Astra's absent-work list and needs its own lane.

body:
Every lane finished by appending a dated `## ` section to the end of its task checklist. Two lanes finishing against the same checklist wrote at the same place, so git called it a conflict **every time** — five for five on `09_persistence_replay_reliability.md` in one round, each the same mechanical keep-both where the answer was never in doubt.

The cost was never the risk of resolving one wrongly. It was that it recurred on every lane forever, and a resolution done by hand thirty times eventually gets done carelessly — on the file that records what shipped.

## It was not a §09 problem

Ten task files carried **38 dated sections** between them. §06 had seven, §04 eight, §04.5 five. §09 only conflicted first because it was busiest; every one of those files was the same conflict waiting for two lanes to touch it.

All 38 moved to `docs/tasks/lanes/<task>/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md`, each opening with a title, a `Task:` line and a `Date:` line. Headings promoted one level; fenced code blocks left alone. **Two new files with different names cannot conflict, in any landing order.**

## Two deliberate choices

**No committed index.** An index is a shared file with a shared append point — it would reintroduce precisely what this removes. The directory listing is the index; `tools/lane_notes.py` renders it on demand.

**The checklists stay.** The `[ ]` and `[x]` items are real task state, and lanes tick distinct lines. That collides rarely, and when it does the collision is *meaningful* and wants a human. Only the dated write-ups moved.

## The check matters more than the migration

`tools/lane_notes.py --check` runs in the `contracts` job and refuses **a task file that has grown a dated `## ` section again** — the habit coming back, which is the actual failure mode. Without it this is a tidy-up that lasts until the next lane forgets its brief, and briefs are written fresh each round.

It also refuses a file not named `<date>-<slug>.md`, one missing its title/`Task:`/`Date:` lines, and a `lanes/<n>/` directory naming no task file.

Verified as a negative, not just a pass: appended a dated section, confirmed the refusal names the file **and line**, restored it, confirmed both a PASS and a byte-identical `shasum -a 256`.

## Evidence

```
./tools/run_tests.sh
state_registry_coverage: PASS -- 54 modules, 352 rows, 681 packed columns checked
4336 test(s), 152719 assertion(s), 0 failure(s)
```

Worth recording: the **first** run in this fresh worktree reported `37 failure(s)` because I ran it before `godot --headless --path godot --editor --quit`. After the import pass the assertion count matches the pre-change run exactly (152719), so all 37 were the documented unimported-resource phantom, not anything here. This change touches markdown, one new Python tool and a CI step.

`decision_numbers` PASS (128 records) · `merge_gate` PASS · `ready07_arithmetic` PASS · `lane_notes` PASS (38 records).

Recorded as [ADR 0135](docs/decisions/0135-lane-records-are-one-file-each.md).

## What this does not fix

`docs/systems_architecture.md` is deliberately **not** split. A memory ledger genuinely is one document, and splitting it would break the arithmetic every validator depends on. That file stays serialised by the dispatcher's ownership rule, which is a slower answer but the correct one.

Replaces #108, closed when `--delete-branch` removed its base on the #106 merge. Same head branch, same commits, retargeted to master.

Two commits: the lane's store, then the integration reconciliation the lane was deliberately not allowed to make.

## The store

Transcribed from the registry's §11 declaration, not designed. Six packed columns at `CAPACITY = 64` in declared ordinal order, plus the two declared scalars. Allocated once in `_init()`; `resize()` appears only in `_allocate_columns()`. `_assert_contracts()` proves the eight keys, ordinals, type codes and SAVE-R09-005's 32-byte stride at construction, so a renumbering edit fails at `_init()` rather than at a save.

Allocate-before-consume (ADR 0059): `_advance_sequence()` is the last statement of `schedule_into()`, so a full / exhausted / non-int32 / non-future refusal leaves the store byte-identical including `_next_sequence`. Day boundaries only via `(tick + 4500) mod 18000` — never `tick % 18000`, which is 06:00.

Ten mutations, all died, one per Godot invocation with a `shasum -a 256` byte-compare between runs.

## The reconciliation

`WorldRuntime.next_event_sequence` moves to EventSchedule ownership: **8 bytes changing owner, not 8 added.** WorldRuntime's I64 row drops 3 columns → 2 (24 → 16), EventSchedule gains a 1-column row (8). Net zero; every ledger total unchanged.

`packed_source_field_count` 530 → **536**. `record_count` stays **582** — §11's eight fields were declared long before a module implemented them.

## Three things the lane got wrong

All from computing against a base that moved underneath it:

| Reported | Actual |
|---|---|
| Ledger at lines 417/418/425 | The injury repair moved them to **434/435/441** |
| Next contract key `C168` | C168–C170 already taken → **C171** |
| `3943 test(s), 0 failure(s)` | On the rebased tree: `4043 test(s), **1 failure**` |

That failure was `test_registry_counts_are_the_ones_the_ruling_reconciled`, pinning `REGISTRY_PACKED_FIELD_COUNT = 530`. The pin now carries its reason — REG-R01 *requires* it to grow, while `record_count` must not move without a ruling.

## Evidence

```
./tools/run_tests.sh
state_registry_coverage: PASS -- 51 modules, 335 rows, 654 packed columns checked
4043 test(s), 139176 assertion(s), 0 failure(s)
```

`ready07_arithmetic` PASS · `merge_gate` PASS · `decision_numbers` PASS · `validate_save_registry_handoff --source-root .` PASS (536 packed fields, 50 owners, 582 records).

SURVIVED_MUTANTS: none

## Scope deliberately not claimed

§11 has **no codec** — nothing encodes or decodes `next_sequence:i64` + N 32-byte records — and **no ruled kind/argument domain**, so `_kind`/`_source_id`/`_arg0`/`_arg1` are validated as int32 storage carrying no meaning. There is no producer, no consumer, and the store is wired into no autoload. No release-save completeness is claimed and §15's digest is not unblocked by this alone.

Neither is a defect in this change, and neither makes it unsafe to merge — this store is additive and nothing depends on it yet. Stating it under `BLOCKED:` previously held the PR, which conflated "unsafe to merge" with "scope not claimed"; that field now means only the former.

Replaces #107, which GitHub closed when `--delete-branch` removed its base branch on the #106 merge. Same head branch, same commits, retargeted to master. That auto-close is a real bug in `tools/auto_merge.py` and is fixed in a follow-up.

Answers "build this whole process — fully automated end to end, with approval for art" and "a prompt to give Astra so it can build its own loop".

Contract: [`docs/automation/README.md`](docs/automation/README.md). Recorded as [ADR 0129](docs/decisions/0129-the-development-loop-stops-only-for-art.md).

## The cycle

`work_queue.json` → `dispatch_plan.py` → subagents with file allowlists → PR from the template → CI → `auto_merge.py` → merged → dependants unblock → repeat. Two side channels feed the same queue: `OPEN.md` for questions only Astra can answer, `art_approvals.json` for things only Brendan can.

| Tool | Refuses |
|---|---|
| `dispatch_plan.py` | Tasks whose owned paths intersect each other or anything `in_flight` **or `review`**. `--validate` also refuses cycles, unknown deps, and art gates with no approval id. |
| `auto_merge.py` | Any PR failing one of four: all checks SUCCESS (not pending), mergeable and not draft, `merge_gate.py` against the **branch's** ledger, all three declarations present and empty. |
| `art_gate.py` | Anything not `approved` by a named human. No `--force`, no env var, no agent-writable path. |
| `astra_inbox.py --check` | A stale `OPEN.md`. |

## Why art is the only stop

Paid generation spends Brendan's money and reverting a commit does not refund it. Visual acceptance is taste — no test asserts whether the badger reads as a badger, and an agent accepting its own art is grading its own work. Decision 0002 separately forbids bulk creature generation before proportion approval.

The `DEVIATIONS`/`SURVIVED_MUTANTS`/`BLOCKED` blocks keep a human in the loop without keeping them in the way: most changes declare nothing and merge untouched. A lane once overruled my brief **correctly**, citing SAVE-LAYOUT-R01 over the instruction I gave it — a script that ranked that would be wrong whichever way it ruled, so it stops and surfaces instead.

## Proven in use since it was written

Five lanes ran through it. It caught a stale test pin, a contract-key collision, three stale ledger citations, and — on PR #112 — **six false positives from its own L2 check**, which is now scoped to one owner with the failing fixture kept as a regression case.

## Bug found while building it

`gh api -f ref=<branch>` sends a **request body**, which a GET ignores — so the ledger fetch silently returned the default branch's file. `auto_merge.py` would have checked master's ledger and called it the PR's. Fixed to a query string, with the reason written beside it.

body:
Stacked on #111 → #110 → #109 → #108 → #106. REQ-SET-124–128/137's project lifecycle as its own store — **not** a second Building store. The Building state machine (BLUEPRINT → BUILDING → ACTIVE, ACTIVE → DEMOLISHING → gone) is driven from here.

Delivery before work; consumption at exactly **one** transition (`begin_work()`); 100%-before / 80%-after cancellation refund floored to milli-U; evacuation before demolition; demolition priced at declared construction WU × 0.25 returning 50% of the original §4.1 cost. Two-phase cancellation and completion, both idempotent on retry, so a failed output publishes nothing.

The 100%/80% and 50% paths **refuse each other** — ARCH-JOB-004's ban on a shared "refund all" helper is structural here, not a comment. `_work_begun` is its own column because it is not derivable from `_remaining_mwu`: a project with full remaining work has not necessarily begun.

## This PR proved my own merge gate wrong

L2 refused it with **six false positives** — `present`, `ref_slot`, `ref_generation`, `type_id`, `phase`, `purpose` — colliding ConstructionIndex against BuildingIndex, FurnitureIndex and RoomIndex. Not one shares a byte.

L2 flags a field written `x` in one row and `_x` in another, on the theory it is one byte budgeted twice. **That holds only within one owner**, which is what the real Injury defect was. §3's index tables name members bare while a store's own section spells them as GDScript does.

Fixed both ways: L2 now compares only rows whose owner labels share a leading token, `test_merge_gate.py` gained the exact false-positive fixture as a regression case, and these rows switched to bare names to match the §3 convention they'd broken.

## Ledger

Three §3 rows, **5,142,528 bytes**. The lane computed its figures against `origin/master`, so all seven identities were wrong for this tree:

| | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Payload | 66968467 | **72110995** |
| Live world | 75357075 | **80499603** |
| Transactional peak | 136109958 | **146395014** |

Live keeps 19,500,397 bytes of headroom. §2.2's existing Construction columns are not re-added or enlarged; the bill tables are 3828 bytes inside §2.3's existing arena and owe no row.

## Mutations: 13, two declared survivors, neither waved through

The five named in the brief all die: M9/M1 (refusal that still consumed / still published), M2+M3 (the 100%/80% boundary — both the fraction *and* its placement), M4 (demolition fraction), M5+M7 (work before delivery), M6 (cancelled construction leaving a live row).

**M12 is unreachable, not untested.** `_refund_policy` is written only by `_policy_for()`, the same function the check runs, so no public call sequence can disagree; its caller is the save decoder, which does not exist. ADR 0088 records the identical caveat for `buildings.verify_room_masks()`.

**M13 is equivalent.** PHASE_READY is reachable today only through complete delivery. The gate is deliberate defence against a decoder writing PHASE_READY over an empty ledger — which is exactly what M7's 30 kills show matters. It was not deleted to manufacture a kill.

**Harness incident, disclosed by the lane and recorded in ADR 0131:** a second harness was launched before the first finished; both mutated the same file, producing one false `MUTATION_NOT_APPLIED` and one inflated kill count. Every contaminated verdict was discarded, the harness took a single-instance lock, and all 13 were re-run from a restored file, reproducing the earlier clean run mutation for mutation.

## What is NOT done

**06.1 is left unchecked and the starter settlement is still empty** — 0 buildings, 0 rooms, 0 furniture, 0 projects, now pinned by a test rather than assumed. No Job and no tick stage: `TICK_STAGE_COUNT` is still **8** and that test is unchanged; nothing calls `add_work_mwu()` yet. The dispatcher integration (PLACE_BLUEPRINT, DEMOLISH, …) is not started.

```
./tools/run_tests.sh
state_registry_coverage: PASS -- 52 modules, 350 rows, 681 packed columns checked
4238 test(s), 142421 assertion(s), 0 failure(s)
```

DEVIATIONS: none
SURVIVED_MUTANTS: M12 unreachable, M13 equivalent — both argued above, neither deleted to manufacture a kill
BLOCKED: none

### Scope not claimed (not merge-blockers)

REQ-SET-128's stored-goods half needs container-by-owner enumeration from `inventory.gd`; the tier-2 demolition basis is unresolved and uses the base §4.1 row at every tier; 06.1 is left unchecked and the starter settlement is still empty. All three are filed in Astra's inbox. None makes this change unsafe to merge — it is additive and nothing depends on it yet.

Merged on Brendan's explicit instruction with the two declared survivors standing: M12 unreachable, M13 equivalent, both argued above.

body:
Stacked on #110 → #109 → #108 → #106. **This is the dependency that was holding all twelve section codecs.** Every one could encode; none could capture from or restore into a live store. Decision 0105 solved it for `entity_directory.gd`; this extends the pattern to the three largest §4 COMPONENT_COLUMNS owners.

`needs.gd` (20 columns), `residents.gd` (19), `jobs.gd` (38 §4 + 4 §5, restored as one transaction). Each publishes `copy_columns_into()`, `restore_columns()`, `last_column_refusal()`, `state_bytes()` and its declared ordinal tables.

`docs/persistence_state_registry.md` and `canonical_state_registry.json` **agree for all three modules** — nothing needed adjudication. The suites re-read the JSON artifact and compare ordinal by ordinal.

## One deliberate departure from 0105

The directory takes six positional buffers. Twenty, nineteen and forty-two do not fit that shape, so the buffers travel in a per-store `Columns` inner class — allocated once to declared extents, one named public field per category-1 column in ordinal order, caller-owned and refilled in place exactly as 0105 requires. Re-verified on 4.7.2 that packed arrays are true references through a class member as well as a local *before* anything was written against the assumption.

## Restore ordering is now enforced, not documented

1. §3 before `residents.gd`; §3 **and** `residents.gd` before `jobs.gd`. A reference the directory does not honour refuses; a JobAgent row on an absent resident refuses.
2. §14 must run after §4 for names. `restore_columns()` installs `_named` and empties every `_name_key`; `unresolved_name_row_count()` returns a count, never a sentinel.
3. `jobs.gd`'s §4 and §5 restore as **one call** — a half-applied pair is not a state the store can hold.

## Five mutants survived, and none were waved through

Three were checks no input could reach, **deleted** with the reasoning written into the docstrings: the worker-binding `named != bound_jobs` comparison; an `agent_present != 1` guard the free-agent-row rule already subsumes; and the generation half of the job→agent reference comparison.

Two were **missing coverage**, and got tests: deleting the *slot* half of that comparison survived until "two live jobs claiming one worker" was added, deliberately on the same directory generation so nothing else separates them; and widening the *negative* need-remainder bound survived a positive-only boundary test — decay leaves negative remainders, so that was the side that mattered.

32 runs over 26 sites, one mutation per Godot invocation, each file `shasum -a 256` byte-compared after every restore. The member-chain step-cap mutant kills by **non-termination**, blowing the harness alarm with no summary line — which is what `test_a_cyclic_member_chain_refuses_instead_of_hanging` is named for, and is recorded as a hang rather than a failure count.

## An environment finding, proved rather than assumed

On the fresh worktree *before* `--editor --quit`, the suite reported `3912 test(s), 36 failure(s)` — and reported the **identical 36-failure set with all three production files reverted to `origin/master`**. All were UI/theme/font suites on unimported resources. That is how you establish "not mine".

## Corrected a stale production comment

`residents.gd`'s header asserted there was no restore writer because inventing one would invent migration provenance. The store half now exists and infers nothing — `_life_stage` arrives in the column set or the call refuses, and no row is repaired to ADULT. Refusing a **pre-column schema** remains the codec's job through `owner_schema_version`, because a store handed a column set cannot see which schema produced it.

## Rebase note

Conflicted on `docs/tasks/09_persistence_replay_reliability.md` — two lanes each appending a dated section. Mechanical keep-both; both survive at lines 501 and 604.

**No ledger byte owed.** Everything published is a reader, validator, refusal code or inner class. Three existing category-3 scratch rows extended for `_last_column_refusal` rather than three new rows added.

```
./tools/run_tests.sh

4188 test(s), 141922 assertion(s), 0 failure(s)
```

No release-save completeness claimed: there is still no §4 COMPONENT_COLUMNS codec and no §5 CHILD_ARENAS codec. These are the store halves only. BLOCKER J2 is untouched — it names `job_planner.gd`, a different module.

body:
Stacked on #109 → #108 → #106. Implements ALERT-R02: NARROW always compact; STANDARD/WIDE prefer the complete text with adaptive fitting and fallback inside the existing zone.

The second alert card is a second **instance** of UI-SET-011, not a new §4 id — §4 catalogues one "Alert card" row and §8.2 lists 011 once. It shares the registry row, hit-test id and accessible role, carries node suffix `alert_card_2`, and its tab stop is spliced at the `Control` level because `ui_focus_order.gd` is keyed on §4 ids and is not this lane's file.

`alert_stack_into` gained an explicit `count`: the shell's measured buffer is preallocated at 2, so `measured.size()` could not express "how many notices want a card" and the second slot rendered as an empty card. Out-of-range refuses with `UI_INVALID_ALERT_NOTICE_COUNT`.

A card prints *exactly* `notice.summary` or *exactly* `notice.message` — no third truncating branch. The accessible description carries the whole message either way.

## Two things measured that the ruling could not have known

Neither was fixed here. Both are premises, and correcting a premise is not an implementation choice — they are now items in Astra's inbox.

**1. The 44px full card is unreachable typography.** ALERT-R02 states two 44px full cards fit exactly in the 92px zone. In the real theme one wrapped line is **23px**, and §1.2's padding is 12px top and bottom, so the smallest possible *full* card is **47px**. A 47px first card leaves 41px — under the 44px minimum — and the second notice is not placed. Captures `36`/`37` show one card where the ruling implies two; `32`/`33`, where card one is a 44px *summary*, show two. The rail states it correctly in both.

**2. §1.2 publishes two rectangles that collide at the supported floor.** At 1280×720 @100% the alert zone `(460, 16, 360, 96)` lies **wholly inside** the workspace/modal frame `(160, 16, 960, 688)`. Same at @150%. At 1920×1080 the frame starts at y=180 and there is no overlap. This is **not** a z-order bug: §3's layer table puts workspace at layer 40 and permanent HUD zones at layer 20, so the workspace drawing over the alert zone is the specification working as written. Both cards are placed correctly and report `visible = true`. Captured as evidence `40`; recorded open in ADR 0134 and the task checklist.

## Evidence

`docs/validation/evidence/ui-refinement/screenshots/`, files `32`–`40`, native macOS, windowed, absolute `save_png` path. The harness supplies **no message text**: the Info line is `main.gd`'s own boot alert and the Error line comes from choosing HOLT in UI-SET-103 and running the real `create_world()`.

Nothing overflows or clips in any capture. Pre-existing and not this lane's: counter cells clip (ADR 0076) and the NARROW command strip overlaps the minimap frame.

Ten mutations, all killed, one Godot invocation each with a `shasum -a 256` byte-compare between runs. M4a/M4b split the required "stack exceeding its zone" mutant so each run mutates one line.

**No new packed column, so no ledger or registry row is owed.**


title: ALERT-R02: two instances of one catalogued card, and two §1.2 premises that don't hold

body:
Stacked on #108 → #106. **Residents render for the first time.** `World/Entities` was empty and nothing consumed `presentation_extract.gd`; now twelve mice draw from a `MultiMeshInstance3D` with 512 instances preallocated in `_init()` and `visible_instance_count` following the living.

Fifteen mutations, all killed, one Godot invocation each with a `shasum -a 256` byte-compare between runs. Two of them — M5 (`is_present` instead of `is_alive`, so the dead keep drawing) and M7 (the filled buffer never reaches the MultiMesh) — were added *after* writing the tests that catch them; the original suite let both through, because despawn clears presence and life together and every other test read the private buffer rather than the MultiMesh.

## What you can see, and what is wrong with it

Untextured white, bind pose with arms out, standing in a rigid straight line. The straight line is not a rendering bug — see below.

The lane predicted the mice would face backwards. **They don't** — the closeup shows them facing the camera. Correcting that here so nobody chases it.

Pre-existing and not this lane's: the HUD still reads `Residents --` and `No world generated` after a successful generation, visible in the before capture too.

## The line is a refusal, not a layout

**No resident in the running game has an authoritative position.** `settlement_system.gd` composes fourteen core stores and `transforms.gd` is not one of them, so nothing calls `place()`. And GDD §5.1 authors no spawn coordinates — only that room assignments follow resident ID ascending and bed ID ascending, and beds need a Furniture store `world_init.gd`'s own header records as BLOCKED.

Writing an invented layout into authoritative state is the invented production constant the movement amendment forbids, so the lane built a presentation-private pose store instead: read by no tick stage, in no save section, all geometry derived from `world_init.gd`. The single unauthored choice — which cleared tile a resident stands on — is isolated in `muster_tile_x/z()`.

It costs **3,151,872 bytes**, 98% of this PR's whole ledger delta, and the row is marked *deleted whole* when movement composes ARCH-SYS-001. Now a blocking question for Astra rather than a commit-message footnote.

## Ledger

| Row | Count | Per | Bytes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Resident crowd instance buffer | 512 | 100 | 51200 |
| Presentation pose scaffold Transform store | 87552 | 36 | 3151872 |

| | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Payload | 63765395 | **66968467** |
| Live world | 72154003 | **75357075** |
| Transactional peak | 129703814 | **136109958** |

Live keeps 24,642,925 bytes of headroom. The peak was already past the gate — that is why ARCH-MEM-006 selected disk-backed rollback.

## Evidence

`docs/validation/evidence/resident-render-path/` — native macOS, windowed, absolute `save_png` paths, plus the before capture at `914444b` showing empty ground. Instance origins `(117.0, 0.5, 139.0)`, `(119.0, …)`, `(121.0, …)`, hand-checkable against §5.9's hall origin and §5.1's tile pitch: `(2048*58+1024)/1024 = 117.0`.

body:
Stacked on #106 (it needs the repaired ledger). Two commits: the lane's store, then the integration reconciliation the lane was deliberately not allowed to make.

## The store

Transcribed from the registry's §11 declaration, not designed. Six packed columns at `CAPACITY = 64` in declared ordinal order, plus the two declared scalars. Allocated once in `_init()`; `resize()` appears only in `_allocate_columns()`. `_assert_contracts()` proves the eight keys, ordinals, type codes and SAVE-R09-005's 32-byte stride at construction, so a renumbering edit fails at `_init()` rather than at a save.

Allocate-before-consume (ADR 0059): `_advance_sequence()` is the last statement of `schedule_into()`, so a full / exhausted / non-int32 / non-future refusal leaves the store byte-identical including `_next_sequence`. Day boundaries only via `(tick + 4500) mod 18000` — never `tick % 18000`, which is 06:00.

Ten mutations, all died, one mutation per Godot invocation with a `shasum -a 256` byte-compare against a pristine copy between each.

## The reconciliation

`WorldRuntime.next_event_sequence` moves to EventSchedule ownership: **8 bytes changing owner, not 8 added.** WorldRuntime's I64 row drops 3 columns → 2 (24 → 16), EventSchedule gains a 1-column row (8). Net zero; every ledger total unchanged.

`packed_source_field_count` 530 → **536**. `record_count` stays **582** — §11's eight fields were declared long before a module implemented them.

## Three things the lane got wrong

All from computing against a base that moved underneath it, all caught by re-deriving instead of transcribing:

| Reported | Actual |
|---|---|
| Ledger at lines 417/418/425 | The injury repair moved them to **434/435/441** |
| Next contract key `C168` | C168–C170 already taken by the registry reconciliation → **C171** |
| `3943 test(s), 0 failure(s)` | On the rebased tree: `4043 test(s), **1 failure**` |

That failure was `test_registry_counts_are_the_ones_the_ruling_reconciled`, pinning `REGISTRY_PACKED_FIELD_COUNT = 530`. The pin now carries its reason — REG-R01 *requires* it to grow (512 → 530 → 536), while `record_count` must not move without a ruling. Confusing the two turns a snapshot into a format constant that refuses every new store.

A green report is only as good as the tree it ran against.

## Evidence

body:
Stacked on #106. Answers "build this whole process — fully automated end to end, with approval for art" and "a prompt to give Astra so it can build its own loop".

Contract: [`docs/automation/README.md`](docs/automation/README.md). Recorded as [ADR 0129](docs/decisions/0129-the-development-loop-stops-only-for-art.md).

## The cycle

`work_queue.json` → `dispatch_plan.py` → subagents with file allowlists → PR from the template → CI → `auto_merge.py` → merged → dependants unblock → back to dispatch. Two side channels feed the same queue: `OPEN.md` for questions only Astra can answer, `art_approvals.json` for things only Brendan can.

| Tool | Refuses |
|---|---|
| `dispatch_plan.py` | Tasks whose owned paths intersect each other or anything `in_flight` **or `review`**. `--validate` also refuses cycles, unknown deps, and art gates with no approval id. |
| `auto_merge.py` | Any PR failing one of four: all checks SUCCESS (not pending), mergeable and not draft, `merge_gate.py` against the **branch's** ledger, all three declarations present and empty. |
| `art_gate.py` | Anything not `approved` by a named human. No `--force`, no env var, no agent-writable path. |
| `astra_inbox.py --check` | A stale `OPEN.md`. |

## Why art is the only stop

Paid generation spends Brendan's money and reverting a commit does not refund it. Visual acceptance is taste — no test asserts whether the badger reads as a badger, and an agent accepting its own art is grading its own work. Decision 0002 separately forbids bulk creature generation before proportion approval. Everything else is arithmetic, behaviour or process.

The `DEVIATIONS`/`SURVIVED_MUTANTS`/`BLOCKED` blocks keep a human in the loop without keeping them in the way: most changes declare nothing and merge untouched. A lane once overruled my brief **correctly**, citing SAVE-LAYOUT-R01 over the instruction I gave it — a script that ranked that would be wrong whichever way it ruled, so it stops and surfaces instead.

## Honest first output

```
DISPATCH NOW (0):
RUNNING (5): ALERT-R02, BULK-COLUMNS, CONSTRUCTION-STORE, EVENT-SCHEDULE, RENDER-PATH
AWAITING MERGE (3): GATE-MERGE, SAVE-S12, SAVE-S7
WITHHELD (7):
  ART-CREATURES        depends on ART-PROPORTION
  ART-PROPORTION       art approval 'ART-PROPORTION' is not approved
  ART-UI-12            art approval 'ART-UI-12' is not approved
  DIGEST-DETERMINISM   awaiting Astra: ...#retired-row-blanking
  MOVE-ENVELOPES       awaiting Astra: ...#move-g01-clearance-and-modes
  SAVE-CAPTURE         depends on BULK-COLUMNS, SAVE-S7, SAVE-S12, EVENT-SCHEDULE
  SAVE-S1-OWNERS       awaiting Astra: ...#w2-section-1-owners-without-encoders
```

Nothing is dispatchable because everything unblocked is already running. A queue that invented work to look busy would be worse than one that says so.

## Bug found while building it

`gh api -f ref=<branch>` sends a **request body**, which a GET ignores — so the ledger fetch silently returned the default branch's file. `auto_merge.py` would have checked master's ledger and called it the PR's. Fixed to a query string, with the reason written beside it.

title: The development loop: continuous dispatch, automatic merge, art asks permission

body:
Answers "can you build something that reviews and catches those merge issues to allow us to automate the merge as well".

`docs/validation/merge_gate.py` runs four checks in the `contracts` job — no engine, no LFS, under a second. Every one is a defect that actually reached a PR here, passed the full Godot suite and every other validator, and was caught only by a human recomputing the arithmetic.

| Check | Refuses |
|---|---|
| **L1** | A trail row whose running payload is not the row above plus its own delta, or whose reserve column is not payload + 8388608. Checked row by row: comparing totals is what let five merges through. |
| **L2** | A field written `x` in one ledger row and `_x` in another — one byte budgeted twice, once under the planned component and once under the store implementing it. |
| **L3** | A ledger row where width × columns × rows ≠ its own byte total. |
| **A1** | An agent report whose `DEVIATIONS:` / `SURVIVED_MUTANTS:` / `BLOCKED:` blocks are non-empty **or missing**. |

A1 does not judge the exception — a lane that overrules its brief may be right, and one was, citing SAVE-LAYOUT-R01 over my instruction. It removes the change from the automatic path so a human reads it.

## L2 fired on its author's own change

Decision 0109 added all eleven of `injury.gd`'s columns to §3 as **+21504**, while §2.2 already carried the Injury component's rows budgeting `kind`, `severity`, `rescuer_slot`, `rescuer_generation` and `care_progress_mwu` at 10240 + 4096. **14336 bytes counted twice.**

The repair moves `injury.gd`'s actual layout into §2.2 — where implemented component columns live, as `residents.gd`'s own `_named`/`_selected` are — and reduces 0109's trail delta to its net **+7168**:

| | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| §2.2 | 142 rows / 25029474 | **144 rows / 25036642** |
| §3 | — | **72 rows / 20150752** |
| Payload | 63779731 | **63765395** |
| Live world | 72168339 | **72154003** |
| Transactional peak | 129732486 | **129703814** |

`ready07_arithmetic.py`'s `DECISION_0109_ADDED` now carries the subtraction with the reason beside it.

## The negative case is a first-class test

A gate that only ever passes is indistinguishable from a gate that does nothing. `test_merge_gate.py` drives all four checks with the defect they exist for *and* with a clean input — eleven cases, including the reduced form of this double budget and the bare-name case (`Building`, `FarmPlot`, `Feast`, `Job` and `RngStream` each legitimately carry their own `state`) that made the discarded first draft emit 84 false positives.

Verified by hand: the gate REFUSES the pre-repair tree with 6 problems and PASSES the repaired one, with `docs/systems_architecture.md` byte-identical by `shasum -a 256` after the experiment.

Recorded as [ADR 0128](docs/decisions/0128-the-merge-gate-and-the-injury-double-budget-it-found.md).
